raw_response:
I will not start from zero. I will do almost what I did last year, then adjust a little by price, labor, and what I saw around me. I have 10.1 mu and only 2 people in the house, so I will keep the main part in the wheat-maize rotation because that is steady and I know the work rhythm well. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because I have grown it many years and I do not want all my income tied to one line. On wheat, I will spend a bit more on base fertilizer and water because if wheat stand is weak in spring, it is hard to pull yield back. On maize, I will do simpler work after wheat harvest, mostly direct or light tillage, because time is tight and labor is short. On cotton, I will not be stingy with potassium and sprays, because cotton looks fine early and then loses yield fast if insects and late weakness come together. I do watch what nearby farmers do, and around here nobody dares cut fertilizer too hard on good irrigated land. Fertilizer costs money, but losing 50 to 100 jin per mu costs more, so I will hold the rates at a level I know can carry yield.
